Hi Naomi / Marcus,

Quick escalation: Sprintly (see details below) is asking for Net-90 payment terms plus quarterly invoicing for the first 12 months. Deal specifics: $420k ARR initially (annualized), they want to consolidate invoices quarterly and remit on a 90-day schedule.

Why they're asking: seasonal revenue/VC cadence. Why this matters to us: this materially delays cash collection and increases credit exposure. Customer has requested a commercial concession in exchange for a longer committed term and a promotional discount.

Mitigations proposed by AE (what customer will accept):
- 30% payment up front at contract signature
- Funds for first quarter held in escrow (third-party) and released on completion of Q1 usage milestone
- Standard SaaS SLA; Redwood retains right to suspend for non-payment

Attachments: Signed_SOW_v3.pdf (application/pdf), Credit_Assessment.xlsx (xlsx)
HubSpot: SPRINT-2387

Asking for: finance + exec approval to present conditional acceptance (Net-90 + quarterly invoicing) with the above safeguards. If we can get an exception, Priyom plans to convert this to a closed-won this week.

Key contacts: Elena Morales (Sprintly, Head of Finance) <elena.morales@sprintly.io> — she is contract owner.

Thanks,

Naomi / Priyom — short finance risk brief attached. TL;DR: Sprintly has a good product-market fit but a thin balance sheet (Series B, cash runway ~10 months). They have several existing suppliers on extended terms and some delayed remittances in the last 6 months.

Recommended conditional package to accept Net-90 + quarterly invoicing: 
1) 30% non-refundable deposit due at signature.
2) First quarter funds placed in escrow with release contingent on usage milestone (as described in SOW).
3) Monthly usage reporting and a finance point-of-contact for reconciliation.
4) 1.5% processing fee on invoices to offset extended float cost.
5) A holdback clause: if payments are late beyond two cycles, Redwood can automatically convert remaining invoices to net-30 and pause services.

If Legal approves the suspension and escrow language we can proceed. I attach: Finance_Risk_Summary.pdf (pdf, 56 KB).

—Marcus
